t.6.43.1: Hearing that Dhūmrākṣa had been slain, Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, spoke these words to the commander of his army, who stood before him with joined palms.
t.6.43.2: Let the invincible Rākṣasas of terrible valor quickly march forth, placing at their head Akampana, who is thoroughly skilled in all weapons.
t.6.43.3: Then the foremost rākṣasas, bearing various weapons, fearful-eyed and terrible to behold, sallied forth, urged on by the commanders of the army.
t.6.43.4: Then Akampana, wearing earrings of refined gold, mounted a large chariot and sallied forth, surrounded by fearsome rākṣasas.
t.6.43.6: As he rushed forward, enraged and eager for battle, a sudden dejection came upon the horses that drew his chariot.
t.6.43.5: For he could not be shaken even by the gods in a great battle; hence he was called Akampana, and among them he was like the sun in his splendor.
t.6.43.7: The left eye of him who delighted in battle throbbed, the colour of his face grew pale, and his voice became faltering.
t.6.43.8: Even on a fair day a dark, stormy gloom arose with harsh, rough winds, and all the birds and beasts uttered cruel cries that struck terror.
t.6.43.9: He, whose shoulders were broad like a lion's and whose valour equalled a tiger's, paid no heed to those portents and went forth to the battlefield.
t.6.43.10: Then, as that rākṣasa went forth together with the rākṣasas, there arose a very great roar, as if churning up the ocean.
t.6.43.12: There arose a most terrible battle between those monkeys and rākṣasas, who had utterly abandoned all care for their lives for the sake of Rāma and Rāvaṇa.
t.6.43.11: Alarmed by that sound, the great army of the monkeys, wielding trees and rocks as weapons, stood firm, ready to fight.
t.6.43.13: For all of them, the monkeys and the rākṣasas alike, were exceedingly mighty heroes, all resembling mountains, each eager to slay the other.
t.6.43.14: In that battle a very great uproar was heard from those exceedingly mighty warriors as they roared and, in their rage, bellowed at one another.
t.6.43.15: And the dust, reddish in hue, became exceedingly dreadful; raised up by the monkeys and the Rākṣasas, it covered all ten directions.
t.6.43.16: On the battlefield the warriors could not see one another, nor the creatures shrouded by that dust, which rose up pale as silk.
t.6.43.17: Because of that dust, neither banner nor flag, nor armour nor horse, nor weapon nor chariot could be seen.
t.6.43.18: In that tumultuous battle a very great uproar was heard from them as they roared and rushed at one another, and their forms could no longer be made out.
t.6.43.19: Then, in the darkness of the battle, the monkeys, greatly enraged, struck down monkeys themselves, and the Rākṣasas too slew Rākṣasas.
t.6.43.20: Striking down their foes and even their own kind, the vānaras and rākṣasas then made the earth wet with blood and smeared with mire.
t.6.43.21: Then the dust, sprinkled by the flood of blood, settled away, and the earth became strewn with bodies and corpses.
t.6.43.22: With trees, spears, rocks and darts, with maces, iron clubs and lances, the monkeys and the rākṣasas swiftly struck one another with great force.
t.6.43.23: Fighting with arms like iron clubs, the monkeys, huge as mountains and terrible in their deeds, slew the rākṣasas in battle.
t.6.43.24: And the Rākṣasas too, greatly enraged, with darts and lances in their hands, struck down the monkeys there with exceedingly terrible weapons.
t.6.43.25: The monkeys too, rushing forward and wresting away their weapons by sheer might, tore the rākṣasas apart with great trees and huge rocks.
t.6.43.26: Meanwhile the heroic monkeys Kumuda, Nala and Mainda, the last filled with supreme fury, launched an unsurpassed onslaught.
t.6.43.27: But those leaders of the monkey troops, of mighty speed, wrought a very great slaughter with trees at the front of the army of the Rākṣasas, as if in play.
